tier3_keyed_diffs.mode: full_diff on every collection; no sampling

anomaly_budget.why: the 37/50/31 anomalies all sit in CUSTOMER_MASTER and INVOICE_LINE, which are wave 1 units

idempotency.proven_by: second full load, no drop, byte-identical target

unverified_or_not_covered: Y/N-to-boolean, CSV-to-array and DD-MON-YY-string-to-date are graded by tier 4 operations, not by the canonicaliser: the harness has no rule for them and patching the harness was out of scope. Raised as profile feedback in .migration/canonicalization.json.
CODES-decoded fields (plans.tier, tenants.status, subscriptions.status) are graded by tier 4 operations, not tier 3, because the source holds integers and the target holds decoded strings.
subscription_history is empty at source (0 rows), so its field grading is structurally exercised but not value-exercised.

The repo self-check asks for an ow_tp / ow-tp- namespace prefix. The engagement intake fixes the target database as ow_billing_migration, so the prefix rule is deliberately not met; the allowlist in .migration/allowed_targets.json is the control instead.
Scale is the demo fixture on an Atlas M0 cluster. Nothing here is a statement about production volumes.
source_access: SELECT/WITH only; no DDL or DML against OW_BILLING
